rootCause.wrongValueObserved: activateManualSubscription with billingPeriodDays 365: "PROBE create.cycle = undefined update.cycle = undefined create.periodEnd-periodStart days = 365". rollCycles on that row (cycle MONTHLY by schema default, externalPayment true, 2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01): "PROBE select = {"tenantId":true,"cycle":true,"periodEnd":true} rolled periodStart = 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z periodEnd = 2026-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", when it should be 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.
rootCause.note:
I reproduced the bug on the current tree with a throwaway Jest probe. It lives only in the scratchpad (scratchpad/rc863/probe.spec.ts) and I ran it with `--roots` pointed there. No repo files were changed.

The named cause is correct on both halves:
1. **Activation never sets `cycle`.** Both branches of the `tenantSubscription.upsert` call in apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.ts (about lines 963-995) leave out `cycle`. I called the real `activateManualSubscription` with `billingPeriodDays: 365` and stubbed dependencies, then captured the upsert arguments: `create.cycle` and `update.cycle` were both `undefined`, and `periodEnd` minus `periodStart` was 365 days. The column defaults to MONTHLY (platform.prisma:47, `cycle BillingCycle @default(MONTHLY)`). So a prepaid annual row is stored as MONTHLY on create and keeps whatever cycle it already had on update.
2. **The cron rolls by `cycle` only.** `rollCycles` in apps/api/src/billing/billing-cron.service.ts (about lines 484-498) selects only `{tenantId, cycle, periodEnd}`. It never reads `periodStart` or `externalPayment`, and it calls `addCycle(start, s.cycle)`, which adds 1 month unless the cycle is ANNUAL. Run on the real service, a 365-day external row (2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01) rolled to periodEnd 2026-02-01, one month instead of a year. That is exactly the wrong value test-plan T3 predicts.

The brief's own check doesn't work. `jest -t "REG-ROLL-MANUAL-ANNUAL"` can't be "green today" because no test by that name exists: grep for MANUAL-ANNUAL and manual-annual under apps/api/src returned nothing. The repro-test task has to write it as REG-B863-ROLL (per the test plan) rather than flip an existing test.

In the probe, `activateManualSubscription` threw after the upsert because my stub had no `findMany`. That doesn't affect the upsert arguments I captured, since they were recorded before the throw. I did not run the probe for 90- or 180-day periods; by the same code path they would also roll +1 month, but that is inferred, not observed.
